findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and no rows get deleted
findings.body: The Prisma delete calls are lazy. They only run at `Promise.all` after the loop. If `client.request` throws for one reminder, for example an already-sent batch or an invalid batch_id, the catch block runs and none of the queued deletes run. That reminder stays `cancelled: true` and fails again on every cron run. It blocks every reminder after it in the list, so those emails are still sent. Handle each reminder in its own try/catch and delete (await) that row right after its cancel succeeds. Skip or delete reminders that fail permanently.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation is not awaited, so the DB update may never finish
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and now do the persistent work: they set `cancelled` or delete the row, and the SMS one also calls Twilio. The old code awaited the DB deletes through `prismaPromises`. The new calls are fire-and-forget, so the handler can return and the serverless function can be frozen before `cancelled: true` is saved. The cron then never sees the reminder and the email is still sent. Collect the promises and await them with the other promises (`Promise.all`). The same applies to the calls in `bookings.tsx` and `workflows.tsx`.
